question: A patient requires an immediately effective, precisely dosed drug with 100% bioavailability. Which route of administration BEST achieves this?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The IV route delivers drug directly into systemic circulation, achieving 100% bioavailability with immediate onset — the reference standard for bioavailability comparisons.
Oral bioavailability is always <100% due to first-pass metabolism and incomplete absorption. Onset is slower and variable.
IM absorption is generally good but not 100% and is slower than IV; it also depends on muscle blood flow and drug properties.
Sublingual avoids first-pass metabolism and has rapid onset, but bioavailability is still <100% and varies by drug (e.g., GTN ~38%).

overallFeedback.feedback: Only the IV route bypasses all absorption barriers, delivering drug directly into the bloodstream for 100% bioavailability.
Correct! IV administration = 100% bioavailability, immediate onset. All other routes involve some absorption step with inherent variability.
